question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil, SIA, is reviewing the pre-registration dossier of Pragati Foundation, an education NPO applying to NSE SSE. She wants to verify that the NPO meets the minimum fund-flow threshold under SEBI ICDR Regulation 292F(1). What is the MINIMUM annual spending (receipts or payments from audited accounts) required in the PAST financial year for NPO registration?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Table 3.1 of the SSE Guidebook (read with Reg 292F(1) of SEBI ICDR Regulations 2018), the NPO must demonstrate Annual Spending of at least Rs. 50 lakhs in the past financial year, evidenced by Receipts/Payments from Audited accounts or Fund Flow Statement. Funding received in the past FY must be at least Rs. 10 lakhs (separate threshold). The Trap: Rs. 10 lakhs is the Funding threshold (not Spending) and is a common swap. Rs. 25 lakhs and Rs. 1 crore are plausible-looking but not in the regulation. The SIA must memorise the two separate limbs — Rs. 50L spending AND Rs. 10L funding — both are cumulative conditions. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C (Compliance) test listing financial thresholds. X-A (IA L1) touches NPO donor-eligibility from a donor-advisory angle but does not test 292F(1) limits. XII (Securities Markets Foundation) treats SSE as a specialised platform and does not drill into 292F. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When verifying the Rs. 50 lakh spending threshold, don't just read the income-expenditure statement — reconcile to the Fund Flow Statement and bank statements. NPOs often book grant-in-advance as liability, so reported 'expenditure' in P&L may understate actual deployment. Trace at least 3 largest programme vouchers to source documents before signing the eligibility note.
